column1: # Test run policy table (issue #407 item 3) — single source of truth for
# per-class QEMU run policy. Consumed ONLY via tools/test-policy.awk
# anywhere else. `|` separator survives editors/formatters (no TABs).
# Tiers, lowest precedence first (later line wins within a tier):
# An arch record beats a group record (riscv64 always 400 s, even heavy).
# `members` rows are resolver metadata (group membership), not policy.
# Each row carries its originating issue as provenance.
# Reserved: `requires|ovmf` key for q35 OVMF guards (deferred follow-up).
group|heavy|members|core_basic core_sync core_sched core_task core_memory core_syscall core_tracing smp_multicpu ahci_live iommu_live deadline
# (2026-10-26) The 43 measured+30pct class rows were REMOVED: their values
# were computed in MILLISECONDS from guest TIME rows but this field is
# consumed in SECONDS (run-test.exp `set timeout`, GNU outer `timeout`,
# meson test() timeouts) - e.g. 15022 meant 4.2 hours, not +30pct. Verified
# by units audit: defaults 120/250/400 only make sense as seconds (a 120ms
# QEMU expect gate could never boot), and the aarch64 testrunner 123s
# EXPECTED_PANIC_PASS equals the 120s default firing. Impact was bounded in
# practice by the host watchdog (220s stall preemption), but every failure
# path paid ~220s instead of the intended budget.
# The arch-qualified class-selector MECHANISM (awk) is retained and valid;
# re-add per-class rows ONLY from measured wall-clock SECONDS (boot +
# suite, not guest TIME_ELAPSED), with the wall source cited per row.
# Until then the tier defaults (120 / 250 heavy / 400 riscv64) apply.
